motivation.problems: Engineers who maintain libraries and backends are handed behaviour that is wrong in many small places and have to find the causes without a safety net. In the diagnosis tasks the repository has lost its tests and a block of symptoms describes many unrelated failures at once, as in aiogram-7a7c3502-blind20-ots, bdwgc-2547e33a-blind27 and libsrtp-32a3a3a5-blind20. In the spec-drift tasks the code still runs but contradicts its own README and docstrings, as in sdrift-sqlglot-sqlglot-003-shared, alembic-canonical and tau-canonical-ots. A third pattern is a single production symptom with a hidden root cause, as in trickster-extentkey-v2 and jsonpatch-movenear-v2. Across all three, the engineer must reproduce the symptom, localize the faulty function, repair it without breaking neighbouring behaviour, and in many tasks say where the defect was.
motivation.how_tasks_exemplify: Each task ships a pinned checkout of a real open-source project, with network disabled at run time and the tests removed or stubbed in the agent's tree. The prompt gives symptoms or a documentation scope but not the location of the faults. The diagnosis tasks ask for /app/rca.json listing file and function per edit, and a separate verifier container restores hidden tests and compares the report to an answer key. The spec-drift tasks keep the documentation as the authority and forbid editing it; the grader runs sealed cases as an unprivileged user and checks that the documentation is unchanged. Rewards combine fail-to-pass repairs with pass-to-pass regressions. Stated fault counts range from 4 in libexpat-realbug-a to 30 in several blind tasks.
prompt_patterns: A first-person list of observed symptoms with a stated number of undocumented edits and a request for /app/rca.json, for example oasdiff-f2d2e121-blind26-ots.
Symptom paragraphs grouped by feature with no file or function named, ending in a fix-and-report request, for example h3-cd62033b-blind21.
A repository description with an explicit in-scope and out-of-scope file list and the rule that documentation is authoritative and must not be edited, for example datatrove-canonical-ots.
A short generic request to restore documented behaviour in a repository, with the docs location given, for example pdk-drift-repository-89042e599dcf.
A single bug report written from a production symptom, with no pointer to the faulty module, for example jsonpatch-movenear-v2.
open_questions: tests/rubrics.json in kafka-python-eaa45b7d-blind29 holds research and planning rubrics. It is not established whether a model or rules score them, or whether they affect the reward.
The h3 task.toml name is h3-17f-687c550d while the catalog name is h3-cd62033b-blind21. The mapping between the two names is not stated.

libexpat-realbug-a is labelled multi-bug diagnosis, but its description says the four defects are real upstream bugs and not injected edits. Confirm whether real-bug tasks belong under the same shape label.

environment_facts: Base image golang pinned by sha256 digest with build-essential and git, CGO_ENABLED=1, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off and -mod=readonly (environment/Dockerfile).

chaisql/chai fetched at commit e53516f8185cac23ea7437592022c5852adc01fd into /workdir. Dependencies are downloaded into /go/pkg/mod and made read-only, and go build ./... is run as the agent (environment/Dockerfile).
A faults/ directory is copied over the checkout, then every *_test.go file and testdata directory is deleted, and the tree is committed as initial import (environment/Dockerfile).
The instruction asks for a _test.go file that runs as a compiled test binary without the repository .go sources present (instruction.md).

The verifier compiles the reproducer and each hidden probe, deletes the .go files under /workdir, then runs the binaries. The existing-suite gate runs go test over the root, sqltests and cmd/chai packages (tests/grade.py, tests/rca-task.json).
Reward is 1 only when reproduce, locate and fix all pass, with a 3000 s verifier timeout and a 21600 s agent timeout and no network (tests/reward_writer.py, task.toml).
tasks.workflow: A database engineer maintains an embedded SQL engine and gets a report that range predicates and descending index scans skip rows from before 2000, although min() and row-by-row reads are correct. The engineer has to find where the engine mishandles these rows, repair it so every query that goes through that code is corrected, add a Go regression test that works as a standalone binary, and name the faulty functions.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A production complaint with two concrete SQL statements and the index definitions, saying results are silently short, with no module named, asking for a library fix, a package test and rca.json.

tasks.name: form-pipeline-ots
tasks.environment_mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["node image pinned by digest with pnpm 12.5.1"] --> B["TanStack Form checkout in /workdir with the drift applied"]
  A --> C["tmux and git on the path, user agent, no network"]
  D["Docs under docs/reference and JSDoc in packages/form-core/src"] --> E["Agent reads docs and code"]
  B --> E
  C --> E
  F["instruction.md: fix drift from the documentation"] --> E
  E --> G["Edited implementation in the workdir, docs untouched"]
  G --> H["Final workdir copied into a separate verifier container"]
  H --> I["Documentation preserved check on pages and doc comments"]
  H --> J["Hidden behavior cases built and run as user nobody"]
  I --> K["Reward written by reward_writer, -1 if the grader crashes"]
  J --> K
environment_facts: Base image node pinned by sha256 digest, with pnpm 12.5.1 installed globally, user agent at uid 1000 and tmux installed for the agent harness (environment/Dockerfile).
The image is built for TanStack/form at commit 2216fdedf0a5ff17e4ef8567e1321442639b96ca and /workdir is a curated tree with the drift applied (environment/Dockerfile).
The documentation in scope is docs/reference and the documentation comments in packages/form-core/src (instruction.md).
The agent has no network and a 21600 s timeout. The verifier is a separate container built from tests/Dockerfile, run as root with a 3000 s timeout (task.toml).
The verifier checks documentation pages by bytes and JSDoc by parsing, then runs each hidden case in its own Node process as nobody (tests/grade_ts.py).
A grader crash leaves reward -1 rather than a behavioral 0 (tests/test.sh).
tasks.workflow: A library maintainer finds that the runtime behavior of the form state and validation core has diverged from its published API reference and JSDoc examples. The engineer reads the reference pages, compares each documented behavior with what the code does, and corrects the implementation without editing the docs or changing the public API. Behavior that already matches the documentation has to stay as it is.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A short brief naming the repository and the documentation in scope, stating that documentation wins over code, forbidding doc edits and API changes, and giving no list of the drifted behaviors.

environment_facts: Toolchain image rust:1.97-bookworm pinned by digest, copied onto buildpack-deps bookworm, with git and tmux installed and user agent at uid 1000 (environment/Dockerfile).
Serde sources are copied to /workdir, dependencies are vendored from a pinned lock file and cargo is set to offline (environment/Dockerfile).
The documentation in scope is rEADME.md, crates-io.md, serde_core/README.md and the doc comments in serde, serde_core, serde_derive and serde_derive_internals (instruction.md).
The agent has no network and a 21600 s timeout. The verifier is a separate container built from tests/Dockerfile, run as root (task.toml).
The verifier checks documentation pages by bytes and Rust doc comments by lexing, then builds a harness of hidden cases as nobody and runs each case in its own process (tests/grade_rs.py).
A case that no longer compiles fails alone, any other build error fails every case, and a grader crash leaves reward -1 (tests/grade_rs.py, tests/test.sh).
tasks.workflow: A library engineer maintaining a serialization framework finds that its derive macros and data model behave differently from what the README and doc comments promise. The engineer reads the documented contract, finds where the implementation departs from it, and restores the documented behavior without editing the docs or altering the public API. Behavior that already matches the documentation must not change.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A short brief naming the repository and the documentation in scope, stating that documentation wins over code, forbidding doc edits and public API changes, and giving no list of the drifted behaviors.
